summary:
Our project is an Arduino-based environmental monitoring system designed to support Mars surface exploration and environmental mapping. It uses a DHT sensor to measure temperature and humidity, while an ultrasonic sensor measures the distance to nearby objects and surfaces.

The system collects sensor readings through an Arduino microcontroller and transmits the data to a dedicated website, where users can monitor and visualize the measurements in real time.

By combining environmental sensing with distance measurement, our solution demonstrates a simple and affordable approach to collecting information about surrounding conditions and physical environments. It aims to support the concept of Martian mapping by providing accessible data that could help understand environmental conditions and nearby terrain features.

The project is important because it demonstrates how accessible electronics, robotics, and web technologies can contribute to future planetary exploration concepts.
details:
Our project is a prototype environmental and distance-monitoring system inspired by the challenges of exploring and mapping the Martian surface. It uses an Arduino microcontroller connected to a DHT sensor and an ultrasonic sensor. The DHT sensor measures temperature and humidity, while the ultrasonic sensor detects nearby objects and measures their distance. These readings are collected and transmitted to a dedicated website, where users can view and monitor the data through a simple, organized interface.

The system demonstrates how environmental measurements and distance detection can be combined to support the concept of robotic exploration and surface mapping. Its main benefits include low-cost implementation, real-time monitoring, easy data visualization, and the flexibility to integrate additional sensors for more advanced exploration tasks.

We developed the prototype using Arduino hardware, a DHT sensor, an ultrasonic sensor, C/C++ for embedded programming, and HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for the website.

Our creative approach is combining environmental sensing, object detection, and web-based visualization in one accessible system. During development, we considered affordability, sensor reliability, measurement accuracy, ease of use, and future scalability. Our intended impact is to demonstrate a practical foundation for robotic environmental monitoring and future planetary exploration technologies.
